state.executionReport:
Implemented the approved Plan `speed-up-load-plan-menus`: the first action menu after selecting a Plan in `/load-plan` no longer waits on durable Session hydration, duplicate publication cleanup, repository-wide Doctor repair, or unscoped transition reconciliation.

**Implementation (all Plan steps done):**
- Removed the eager Session rename on selection; `plan-session-surface.ts` now exposes a one-shot idempotent `activateForPlan(planName)` (terminal title + durable rename, exactly once) replacing `rename`. Continuation actions (resume, review, proceed, planner re-review, direct review, Epic slicer, on-hold resume/reset, recovery continuation/restart) call it right before their workflow work; view/cancel/archive/hold/User-Verified/child-browsing stay rename-free. Epic child naming defers to the child that actually continues.
- Picker runs saved publication-cleanup discovery once; the selected Plan no longer pays for it again (`publicationCleanupDone`).
- `handlePlanRecovery` no longer calls `runPlansDoctor`; its first menu uses one bounded selected-Plan snapshot (read-only `resolveRecoveryWorktree`, scoped journals, one cached Git probe, physical-loss, selected publication proof). Git/physical-loss facts are cached across re-prompts and invalidated only after a non-inspect action.
- `reconcileTransitionRecoveryRecords` accepts an optional `planName` filter applied before effect proof and before `apply` deletes journals; `healSettledTransitionRecords` gets an empty-record fast path that skips the registry read and `git worktree list` entirely. Unscoped callers keep repository-wide behavior.

**Tests added (+7, none removed):**
- `transition-recovery.test.ts` (new, 2 tests): empty selected-Plan journal set heals with Git unavailable; healing one Plan cannot delete another Plan's settled journal.
- `index.integration.test.ts` (4 tests): select+cancel and view+cancel leave a real persisted managed Session's committed generation/transcript byte-length/digest/name unchanged at the menu boundary; resume renames the Session to the Plan; `activateForPlan` renames exactly once across repeated calls.
- `plan-recovery-flow.test.ts` (1 test): cancel at the first recovery menu leaves an unrelated settled journal byte-for-byte unchanged and runs no `for-each-ref`/`clone`/`fetch` (Git Trace2).

**Mutation-verified (tests fail against the old behavior, pass against the fix):**
- Re-adding the eager rename makes the two cancel/view integration tests fail (generation increments).
- Re-adding `runPlansDoctor` makes the recovery test fail (Doctor deletes the unrelated journal).
- Removing the `planName` filter/fast path makes both transition tests fail (Git spawned; other Plan's journal deleted).

**Verification results:**
- Targeted: `index.integration.test.ts` + `plan-recovery-flow.test.ts` + `transition-recovery.test.ts` → 49 tests pass, exit 0.
- `deno task seams:check` → baseline holds (0 seams).
- `deno task check` (types), `deno task lint`, and `deno fmt --check` → clean.
- Full `deno task ci` → all pre-test checks green and **370 test files passed, 0 failed**.

Note: the post-cancel agent restore (`switchAgent` back to the same agent) still publishes a generation — pre-existing behavior outside this Plan's scope. The menu-boundary tests capture evidence at the action-menu prompt to isolate the hot path from it; I stored a project memory documenting that trap.
